newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says WTO report threatens poor banana exporters.
newsitem.headline: EU says WTO report threatens poor banana exporters.

text.p: African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) banana exporting countries face economic ruin if the world Trade Organisation (WTO) forces the European Union to end import benefits, a European Commission spokesman said on Wednesday.
The spokesman was commenting on a WTO trade disputes panel interim report on Tuesday that EU banana import quotas violated open trading rules.

"Obviously any changes to the banana regime would have very serious social, political and economic implications for the ACP banana producing countries," Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely said.
Caribbean countries would be the worst affected.
Kiely said the Commission was carefully studying the WTO report which was only the first of four potential steps before a final decision is taken, possibly in August.
The Commission, along with other parties involved, will prepare comments after which the WTO will take a final decision, against which an appeal could be made.
"The EU banana regime was introduced to create a level playing field for the ACP producers while recognising our international obligations," Kiely added.

In Geneva, diplomats said on Tuesday the unpublished WTO report in effect supported a complaint by the United States and four Latin American states that the EU regime discriminated against their marketing companies and producers.

The report, issued after nearly 10 months of deliberations, recommended that the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) ask Brussels to bring the regime into line with its obligations under global trade accords.
